'''Vampyre Juveniles''' are the lowest rank and first transformation stage of vampyres who were once human. The ones in the [[Burgh de Rott Woods]] can be damaged with any weapon, and the ones in [[Meiyerditch]] require a [[Silver weapons|silver]] or [[blisterwood]] weapon to damage, making them similar to a [[Vampyre Juvinate|juvinate]]. If players use a [[Guthix balance]] potion on them, one of three things can occur: they can be killed instantly, turned into an [[angry vampyre]], or turned back into a [[Former vampyre|human]] and give the player a small reward.

If a Guthix balance potion is not used on the ones in Meiyerditch, then the Juvenile will say "Ha ha, time to disappear and re-rejuvenate!", turn into a cloud of mist and float away when it reaches approximately 0 health. No drops will be received when this happens.

==Trivia==
[[File:Rod of ivandis special.gif|right|frame|Retainer, the [[rod of ivandis|Rod of Ivandis]]'s currently removed special attack used on a Vampyre Juvenile.]]
* Vampyre Juveniles in Burgh de Rott and the Vampyre juveniles in Meiyerditch used to be significantly different, the latter having a much older, albeit unique, model, despite being released later. The [[Update:Temple Trekking: Revamped|graphical updates]] to Morytania and vampyres solved this, making the two look generally the same. The combat levels and capitalisation have also remained different.
* Vampyre juveniles in Temple Trekking would turn into [[Benjamin]], [[Liam (Temple Trekking)|Liam]], [[Miala]], or [[Verak]] if cured by [[Guthix balance]] before an [[Update:Evolution of Combat: Now Live!|update]].
* Vampyre Juveniles may be based on Count Orlock, the main antagonist of the 1924 silent vampire film ''Nosferatu'' (which was criticised for plagiarising Bram Stoker's 1897 novel ''Dracula''), given their bald heads as well as the males' fangs replacing their upper front teeth rather than their upper canine teeth.
